text:
Rina: Ran into a confusing onboarding failure with the monorepo Next + LlamaIndex starter when using the eval harness. Sharing notes.
Owen: repro steps?
Rina: Clone monorepo starter (packages/sample-next-llama), pnpm -w install, build workspace, deploy to Vercel (Edge) or run vercel dev --edge. Set RW_API_KEY. Then run `node ./tools/run-eval.js`. The harness times out waiting for a stream and some requests get 401s unexpectedly.
Max: Which SDK + sample versions?
Rina: @redwood/sdk@0.9.2, sample commit a1b2c3 on main. Next 13.4.8 in the workspace.
Sana: Any stack traces or logs?
Rina: Minimal logs: 
```
> eval-runner starting
WARN sdk: auth cache miss, attempting refresh
Error: Eval harness: stream never opened
    at EvalRunner.waitForStream (packages/tools/eval/runner.js:67:15)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:93:5)
```
Rina: Also saw intermittent 401s on the first request after refresh: the refresh call returns a new token but the immediate following request still gets 401 until the next retry.
Owen: Monorepo nuance: sample runs SDK from workspace via pnpm link/workspace protocol. We had a packaging mismatch where the ESM build shipped a tiny shim that expects a Node global, but Edge runtime provides web globals. Mixed runtimes can break platform detection.
Max: Sounds like two things: (1) streaming transport selection wrong in bundle, (2) auth refresh visibility across module boundaries in monorepo linking.
Sana: Repro tip: replace the workspace SDK import with the published package in the sample (npm i @redwood/sdk@0.9.2) and see if the issue goes away. If it does, it's a build/packaging problem.
Rina: I tried that and the stream issue reduced, but still saw the 401-on-first-retry.
Owen: For the auth race, likely token cache is per-module instance. In monorepos with hoisted deps the sample and SDK may have separate copies of the auth store if the resolution differs. That could cause one copy to refresh while the other still has stale token.
Max: Workarounds: ensure single resolved copy by pinning package manager config or use a request-scoped token provider passed into SDK init. We should make the sample show the request-scoped pattern for monorepos.
Sana: Also the stream fallback: SDK should prefer platform-native ReadableStream/TransformStream if available and avoid bundling a Node polyfill. We'll add a runtime detection that logs which transport is chosen so samples can debug.
Rina: I pasted the minimal failing handler into the created issue: 
```js
import { init, openAgentStream } from '@redwood/sdk'
export default async function handler(req) {
  await init({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
  const stream = await openAgentStream(req.body)
  for await (const chunk of stream) {
    // process
  }
  return new Response('ok')
}
```
Rina: Note I use await init(...) in the sample already. The monorepo duplicate-module case is the likely culprit.
Owen: I'll add a quick script to check node_modules resolution across packages and print resolved paths for @redwood/sdk in each package. That should prove the duplicate-copy hypothesis.
Max: I'll work on SDK change: add an optional tokenProvider override in init({ tokenProvider }) so hosting apps in monorepos can pass a shared provider. Also add a log line showing transport choice.
Sana: I'll update the sample README to include a troubleshooting section for monorepos and a suggested pnpm workspace resolution snippet to force a single copy.
ops-bot: Created incident note: MONO-1345: "monorepo starter - duplicate SDK copy causes auth/stream flakiness".
devex-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-2044 assigned to @Max and @Sana.
Rina: Added bundle listing + package-lock snapshot to the ticket. Also ran the resolution script Owen mentioned and attached output. Two copies of @redwood/sdk resolved in different package roots.
Owen: Confirmed duplicate copies. I'll open a tiny sample PR to show using the tokenProvider pattern and a follow-up PR to the SDK to support it.
Max: I'll prototype the tokenProvider interface today and add a test for monorepo resolution with two module instances.
Rina: Thanks all. Once PRs land I'll re-deploy and validate the eval harness.
Sana: Nice repro + logs, huge help.
Rina: :thumbsup:
